title: International Economics Adventure 2: BoP & Exchange Rates
welcome_lead: Today you'll balance the balance of payments and ride the exchange rate.
meta_desc: Economics: balance of payments (current, capital, financial) and exchange rate determination.
final_note: You read a BoP statement and traced how exchange rates move and affect the economy.

concepts.def: Currency price set by market supply / demand
Currency rises under a floating regime
Depreciation worsens CA before improving it

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Balance of Payments records all transactions with the world.

Current: goods, services, primary income (wages, dividends), secondary income (remittances, aid).
Capital: capital transfers, non-produced non-financial assets.
Financial: FDI, portfolio investment, reserve assets.

By accounting identity, total balance = 0.

Floating: market-set (USD, EUR, GBP).
Fixed: pegged to anchor (HKD to USD).
Managed float: market with intervention (CNY).

Drivers of demand: exports, inward FDI, speculation, interest rates.

A depreciation lowers Px (foreign) and raises Pm (home).

If demand is inelastic short-term, the current account first worsens before improving — the J-curve.

Marshall-Lerner: |PEDx| + |PEDm| > 1 needed for depreciation to improve CA in the long run.
